messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH: Increased 95th percentile latency for /v1/generate observed in prod us-west-2. Incident INC-2026-042. Page sent to #incidents and @eng-oncall.
Ana (eng-oncall): I'm on it. Grabbed initial graphs. 95p jumped ~2.2x at 14:07 UTC. No errors in errors-5m yet, mostly latency.
Mike (eng-runtime): Noted. Any recent rollouts? I see a canary push earlier to canary-pool: model v2.3.1 -> traffic 10% at 13:55 UTC from deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: canary-pool -> v2.3.1 (10%) by CI/CD pipeline at 2026-02-19T13:55:12Z.
Chris (eng-ml): Sharing quick canary diffs I pulled from logs. v2.3.1 seems to have longer decoding steps for longer prompts.
Chris (eng-ml): ```
# sample latency tail (ms) for 2048-token prompt
v2.2.9 95p: 420ms
v2.3.1 95p: 940ms
# CPU/GPU timeline shows higher GPU compute time per token
```
Ana (eng-oncall): Timeline build — adding notes here. Can people confirm times for observed spike:
- 13:54 UTC: normal baseline
- 13:55 UTC: canary rollout -> v2.3.1 (10%)
- 14:07 UTC: 95p latency increase
- 14:12 UTC: customer complaint (SaaS customer A) reported degraded interactive latency
- 14:25 UTC: oncall triage thread opened
Kevin (eng-sre): Logs from edge show routing to fallback model attempts increasing. Sample error snippet:
```json
{"req_id":"abc123","model":"v2.3.1","stage":"decode","latency_ms":1250}
```
Eva (cust-sre): Customer A reports timeouts on chat. Impacted sessions ~0.8% of their active users, but high business impact (support P1). Sasha, fyi.
Sasha (product): Acknowledged. We need mitigation quickly — reduce customer impact then investigate root cause.
Mike (eng-runtime): Hypotheses:
H1: v2.3.1 introduced a decoding change causing worse attention memory compaction -> higher per-token compute at long sequences.
H2: Autoscaler misconfigured for canary pool leading to saturation under bursty traffic.
H3: Deployment accidentally used a different quantization profile (FP16->int8 fallback) for v2.3.1 in canary nodes.
Chris (eng-ml): Evidence: model perf profile shows 2x step time for long sequences in v2.3.1. Also weight layout change noted in build manifests.
Mike (eng-runtime): Quick checks I ran:
- node metrics not OOMing
- GPU util on canary nodes spiked to 98% at 14:05
- request queue length on canary replicas climbed
So H2 and H1 both plausible.
Ana (eng-oncall): Mitigation options: 1) Rollback canary to v2.2.9 (immediate), 2) Increase canary capacity (scale up), 3) Re-route high-latency customers off canary.
Decision? We should minimize customer-visible impact now.
Sasha (product): Prioritize rollback for safety. Do it canary-first then observe main traffic. Notify customers.
Kevin (eng-sre): I'll run the rollback. Command:
```
redwoodctl rollout set canary-pool --model v2.2.9 --traffic 10%
redwoodctl rollout verify canary-pool
```
Mike (eng-runtime): Also pin config to prevent auto-promote: `redwoodctl config set canary-pool.prevent_auto_promote true` until RCA done.
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by Kevin at 2026-02-19T14:18:03Z. Rolling canary back to v2.2.9.
Ana (eng-oncall): Noted. Informing customer-facing channels and support.
Eva (cust-sre): Sending interim customer message: "We're seeing a service degradation impacting interactive latency; engineering has rolled back a recent model canary and is monitoring. We'll update within 30m." Sending now.
Chris (eng-ml): After rollback metrics (first 5min): 95p down to ~430ms at 14:27 UTC. Looks promising.
Ana (eng-oncall): Monitoring: watchlist -> request latency, error rate, queue length on canary nodes, and customer A health endpoint. All checks every 1m.
Mike (eng-runtime): Action items captured in-thread:
- [DONE] Rollback canary to v2.2.9 (Kevin)
- [IN-PROGRESS] Pin canary auto-promote (Mike)
- [OPEN] Gather model build diffs and quantization artifacts for v2.3.1 (Chris)
- [OPEN] Run load repro of v2.3.1 on isolated staging with long-seq prompts (Ana)
Chris (eng-ml): Quick artifact check shows v2.3.1 build used an experimental attention kernel flag `--attn-opt=chunked` in CI. Adding to hypothesis list H4: new kernel optimization regresses long-seq latency.
Ana (eng-oncall): Kicking off RCA doc skeleton here for timeline + evidence. Everyone drop short notes with timestamps/hypotheses.
Kevin (eng-sre): Confirmed rollback completed at 14:22 UTC. No elevated OOMs seen. Will keep autoscaler thresholds conservative till we confirm.
Sasha (product): Thanks team. Once we have root cause, we need to decide on release gating for kernels/attn flags. No more auto-promote for >=minor releases.
Chris (eng-ml): I'll attach diff of attention kernel call sites and perf microbench in the RCA doc.
Ana (eng-oncall): Closing incident pager for now — severity downgraded as latency recovered. Keeping this thread open for RCA coordination. Marking incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager closed by Ana at 2026-02-19T14:35:02Z.
Mike (eng-runtime): Next steps: repro in staging, confirm H4, add a pre-release perf check for long-seq 95p, and update release checklist to include kernel opt review.
Eva (cust-sre): I'll follow up with customer A and confirm SLA impact/reimbursement path if needed. Draft message ready for Sasha review.
Ana (eng-oncall): Great. If anyone adds new logs or hypotheses, paste here. We'll convert to the formal RCA doc after additional data. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
